tier: DNS hosting, no query fees, USD 1 minimum monthly account usage

free_tier.stated: DNS hosting has no charge of its own for up to 500 zones per account and no per-query fee, but the account-wide USD 1 minimum monthly usage applies while a zone is active, so a DNS-only account pays USD 1 a month; a 14-day trial with trial credits and no payment card comes first

per_object_cap.stated: 5,000 records per zone and 500 zones per account by default; both can be raised on request to sales

retention.stated: a trial account is disabled when the trial ends unless the balance is topped up; a negative balance disables the account and after 60 days the stored data is deleted

interface_detail: the bunny.net REST API v3 with an AccessKey header: PUT /dnszone/{zoneId}/records adds a record and POST /dnszone/{zoneId}/records/{id} updates one; no dyndns2 or other HTTP-GET update URL is documented in the pages read, so a dynamic update is a REST call with the record id
tooling: curl against the REST API, the bunny CLI command bunny dns for zones and records, and BIND zone-file import
chaining: scriptable DNS records answer queries with logic, and custom nameservers on the user's own domain are included at no extra cost

limits.value: 5,000 records per zone and 500 zones per account

binding_note: no limit kind binds; a DNS-only account is charged the USD 1 monthly minimum, and a trial account is disabled when the trial ends unless funds are added

identity_cost.detail: trial sign-up needs an e-mail address confirmed by a link, and the trial credits come with no payment card; after the trial the account is disabled unless funds are added, by card, PayPal or crypto, from USD 10 (https://bunny.net/docs/quickstart.md, https://bunny.net/docs/billing/add-funds.md)

reliability_note: an account whose trial has ended or whose balance is negative is disabled, and a disabled account does not keep its zones online; the stored data is deleted 60 days after a negative balance
confidence_note: the DNS pricing page, the DNS and billing documentation, the limits page and the API reference were read and quoted; no sign-up form was submitted, so whether DNS zones can be created before the trial credits are used is as documented, not measured
